tools.name: start_service_request
tools.description: Use this immediately when the user asks to book a supported local service. Pass the complete user intent and every public service detail already stated. The tool determines the vertical, creates the server-side request, and returns a vertical-specific introduction plus either one intake field batch

tools.name: update_service_request
tools.description: Use this for the user's partial response to the current intake or matching batch. Pass only values the user supplied plus selected_time_key when chosen. Fields absent from answers are treated as omitted for that prompt batch; optional and conditionally required omissions do not block progress. Alway

tools.name: get_service_options
tools.description: Use after intake required fields are known, or to refresh matching data. It returns live aggregated potential windows and the current refinement batch without company names. It does not select a provider or reserve capacity.

tools.name: render_service_request_form
tools.description: Use only when update_service_request returns next_action=render_service_request_form. It opens the one final card containing exact provider options, booking fields, policies and Confirm. Do not ask for contact PII in chat.

tools.name: select_service_option
tools.description: Use only from the final protected card when the user selects one exact provider option. It rechecks availability, releases any previous selection, creates one temporary hold for the selected company, and returns its protected booking schema. It does not create a booking.

tools.name: create_service_booking
tools.description: Use only from the protected final card with its one-time authorization after the user presses Confirm. tools.name: complete_account_link
tools.description: Compatibility-only completion for an explicitly initiated legacy profile-link session. Never call it as part of a new booking and never ask for an SMS code in chat. Viewing or managing an existing appointment starts Connect through the corresponding booking-management tool.

tools.name: list_my_service_bookings
tools.description: Use immediately when the user asks to see or manage appointments. For cancellation or rescheduling, pass status='active'. tools.name: get_my_service_booking
tools.description: Open an appointment that belongs to the connected customer. This is read-only. Historical appointments have no available management actions; a current manageable appointment can provide the protected card for exact reschedule or cancellation review.

tools.name: prepare_service_booking_change
tools.description: Use this only from the protected management form after secure appointment access. It prepares the exact reschedule or cancellation review but does not change the booking. tools.name: reschedule_service_booking
tools.description: Use this only with the one-time approval issued after the user confirms the exact reschedule inside the protected management form. It moves the existing booking to the reserved available time, preserves its prior-time history, frees the old capacity, and sends transactional notifications. Safe retri

tools.name: cancel_service_booking
tools.description: Use this only with the one-time approval issued after the user confirms the exact cancellation inside the protected management form. It cancels only the authorized active booking, frees its capacity, and sends transactional notifications. Safe retries must reuse the same idempotency key.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "create_service_booking" references sensitive artifacts (authorization). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

findings.title: Description uses pressure/override language
findings.detail: Description of "list_my_service_bookings" stacks urgency/override words (immediately, never). Legitimate tool descriptions rarely pressure the model to act or ignore prior guidance.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: list_my_service_bookings, get_my_service_booking · Private data: start_service_request, render_service_request_form · Public sink: start_service_request, complete_account_link · Destructive: prepare_service_booking_change.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: list_my_service_bookings, get_my_service_booking · Private data: start_service_request, render_service_request_form · Public sink: start_service_request, complete_account_link · Destructive: prepare_service_booking_change

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
